# STATUS

Last updated 2026-09-14.

## Where the project stands

V1 shipped and the Room Deviation finding is null. The pre-registered 1.5 SD flag (ADR
0008) flagged 10 of 15 linemen, but simulating a homogeneous room with no atypical
athlete by construction flags 69% at that threshold, central 90% interval 7 to 13. The
observed 10 sits inside that interval and carries no information. At stricter
thresholds the room is less extreme than chance. No lineman deviates from the room
beyond normal variation.

The threshold was deliberately not retuned. Any future flagging rule has to be
calibrated against a homogeneous-room null before use, because the statistic is a
maximum over nine categories.

What survives is at room level and is weak: within-category spread matches the general
population (mean SD 0.98), only visual learning approaches a difference from the
NFL-prospect norm (z=-0.40, p=0.009) and that does not survive Bonferroni correction
across nine comparisons, and the room composite sits at the 44th percentile.

`docs/handoffs/2026-08-16-v1-shipped-null-finding.md`. Read both before citing any

=========== Weekly_Research_Review
# STATUS

Read this first. Update it before ending every session.

## Current state
- **2026-09-20: PR #7 is MERGED — the 3-slide readout is a shipped format, not a
  draft.** Verified before merging rather than after: `node tools/build.js
  reviews/001_alignment-jumpers-knee` exits 0 and writes **both** formats
  (`_v4_light`, `_v4_dark`, `_v4_readout_light`, `_v4_readout_dark`, plus
  `teams_v4.md` and `email_v4.txt`), and `reviews/000_sample` — which has **no**
  `readout` block — builds exactly the two original decks and nothing else. So the
  "leave the block out and nothing changes" claim is measured, not assumed. Merging
  publishes nothing on its own. Main at `d152c01`.
- **2026-09-21: #002 (Funakoshi et al. 2024, thoracic outlet syndrome in overhead
  athletes, PR #8) is verified and cleared to send.** The paper is in Zotero as
  `VPXHXK4I`, and review.json now carries that key. It was checked against the paper
  with the printed-page verifier fix (`TypeSafe_Sandbox` PR #19): **28 verified, 2
  review, 0 fabricated or contradicted.** Both review items (the sample line and "two
  thirds excluded or lost") were read by hand against the paper and are supported
  (pp. 620, 624-625).
  - 7 citations were corrected. They cited the page that discusses a table, not the
    page where it is printed: Tables III and IV are on p. 627, Table II on p. 626,
    and the 91.1 and 62.8 percent result is on p. 625. notes.md now uses the same
    printed pages.
  - `trust.design` said "case series". It now says "retrospective cohort comparison",
    matching the paper's own label (Level III, p. 620).
  - Cleared to send by Eric on 2026-09-21. v1 on Drive (published 2026-09-18) carries
    the wrong citations and is superseded by v2 (`version: 2` in review.json).
  - Paper: Funakoshi T, et al. JSES Int 2024;8(3):620-9, PMID 38707577, DOI
    `10.1016/j.jseint.2023.12.004`.
- 2026-09-16: project created and pipeline built (Windows). Intake decisions are in `docs/handoffs/2026-09-16-research-in-5-setup.md`; deck design history in `docs/handoffs/2026-09-16-deck-redesign-and-skill.md`.
- Deck template (merged, PR #4): distilled dark "telemetry" theme plus a light twin, built every run. Baylor Bears Font for display, Agency FB for reading text. One idea per slide; detail lives in the Teams post and email. Eric prefers dark.
- #001 Saraee et al. 2026 (jumper's knee alignment): **v4 is current and ready to send** (`RI5-001_alignment-jumpers-knee_v4_dark.pdf`, `teams_v4.md`, `email_v4.txt` on Drive `07_EDUCATION/Research_in_5/001_alignment-jumpers-knee`). v1 to v3 kept alongside.
- Skill `/research-in-5` (repo erash11/claude-skills) routes into this repo from anywhere; synced to Codex.
- 2026-09-18: #002 v1 built and published to Drive `07_EDUCATION/Research_in_5/002_thoracic-outlet-overhead`. QA PASS on all ten slide images, Agency FB embedded in both PDFs. Came out of the TOS evidence review in `DEV/TOS_Evidence_Brief`. Superseded by v2, see 2026-09-21 above.
- 2026-09-18: **3-slide executive readout** added as an optional second format (branch `worktree-three-slide-readout`, draft PR #7). Add a `readout` block to review.json and build.js also writes `_readout_dark/_light` decks: context, finding, recommendation. Same theme, same fonts, same validator. Spec in `docs/CONTENT_SPEC.md`.
- #001 readout is **published to Drive** (`_v4_readout_dark/_light`, pptx + pdf) alongside the five-slide v4. Publishing also refreshed the v4 five-slide files from the same review.json: content unchanged, all 5 slides re-read after the build.js refactor to confirm it.
- Codex verified the readout's finding and recommendation against notes.md and returned FAIL on four counts, all fixed: do-level verbs against a Preliminary rating, treating a within-player design as evidence about predictive screening, "one team" (it was clubs in one Iranian province), and a p. 8 citation that belonged to p. 3.

- 2026-09-19: **the deck is now verified against its paper before it can publish.**
  `tools/verify.ps1` wraps the deliverable verifier from the `TypeSafe_Sandbox` repo
  (not copied in - a second copy would drift), and `publish.ps1` runs it before the
  Drive copy and refuses on a real finding. `-SkipVerify` overrides it.
  - Three outcomes, matching this project's existing QA vocabulary: **PASS** (exit 0,
    and it names any `[REVIEW]` claims a person still has to read), **FAIL** (exit 1,
    blocks), **DEGRADED** (exit 2, warns and lets the publish through).
  - **DEGRADED deliberately does not block.** The check needs a sibling clone, a venv,
    a key and a network; a gate that stops the week's deliverable because a different
    repo is missing is a gate that gets deleted. WORKFLOW.md requires reporting it.
  - Measured on review 001 against the live API: **PASS in 1.5 s**, 60 verified and 7
    to a person, exit 0. With the sample size corrupted 22 to 93 in `results.stats`:
    **FABRICATED, exit 1, blocked.** With the verifier hidden: **DEGRADED, exit 2, not
    blocked.** Both scripts parse clean.
  - **The locator walks up to find `TypeSafe_Sandbox` instead of assuming it sits one
    level up.** AGENTS.md tells a background session to work in `.claude/worktrees/`,
    where the parent is `.claude/worktrees`, not DEV - assuming the depth would have
    broken the check in the setup this project uses most.
  - Limit worth knowing: only claims that **cite a page** take the numeric string-match
    path. A fabricated number in uncited prose (`did.facts`, `trust.sample`) goes to the
    prose path and can land in `review` rather than `fabricated`. Found while testing
    this wiring; it is a property of the verifier, not of the gate.
  - The skill's three copies (`.claude`, `.agents`, `.codex`) were all patched. They are
    independent files on Windows, not symlinks - confirmed by inode.

## Next
- #002: PR #8 merged and **v2 published 2026-09-21** (publish gate re-verified 28/2,
  Agency FB embedded; `_v2` files on Drive beside v1). Eric posts the v2 dark PDF
  + `teams_v2.md` in Teams and sends `email_v2.txt` to training staff. Send only the
  `_v2` files: v1 carries the wrong page citations. Keep in mind it
  touches a live staff question about softball TOS, and the paper has only 3 softball
  athletes.
- Eric: look at `RI5-001_alignment-jumpers-knee_v4_readout_dark.pdf` on Drive and decide whether the readout is a per-paper option, a replacement, or a one-off. Open question on it: the 5-slide deck is staff education, the readout names an owner and a decision, and not every paper carries one. The format pushes toward a confident recommendation while the evidence rubric pulls the other way; every Codex finding came from that pressure.
- Decide on the five-slide v4 `results.stats[1]` ("<1°", "biggest gap between knees", p. 6). Codex flagged the readout's version of that line as a computed number. The authors do state "less than one degree" in words on p. 6, so it is defensible, but the "biggest gap" framing is ours. The readout now uses the authors' wording; v4 still uses ours.
- Eric: post #001 v4 dark PDF + `teams_v4.md` in Teams; send `email_v4.txt` to training staff.
- Next paper: `/research-in-5` or follow docs/WORKFLOW.md. Give it number 003.
## Open questions
- Does Teams keep the `**bold**` markdown when teams.md is pasted? If not, switch teams.md to plain text like email.txt.
- Email distribution list for training staff outside Teams: who is on it?
- Send day each week?

## Gotchas
- Real validator limits are tighter than docs/CONTENT_SPEC.md states in three places: `trust.design` 45, `trust.sample` 60, chart row `label` 22. build.js is the authority; the spec text is stale.
- Europe PMC `fullTextXML` is a good source when a PMC paper blocks scripted PDF download. It carries every table. Say in notes.md that pages are journal pages, not PDF pages.
- **`review.json` needs `paper.zotero_key` or the verifier cannot run at all.**
  `verify.py` exits immediately on an empty key, so a review built from a source that
  was never imported — like #002, built from Europe PMC XML — silently has no gate at
  all. An ungated deck looks exactly like a passing one from the outside.
- **The TOS "priority four" are the brief's sources, not Research in 5 #002's.**
  #002 runs on Funakoshi, PMID 38707577, which is in `PMIDS_ALL.txt` and not in the
  four. Importing "the TOS papers" the obvious way does nothing for this deck.
- A new paper can be in Zotero before its PDF is indexed. Run `sync_zotero_library` with `include_fulltext: true` and check the item's attachments before falling back to the abstract.
- Slide-facing fields have tight limits (question 90, fact 26, summary 110, role line 70, takeaway 60, bottom line 55). Write them short first; nuance goes in post-only fields.
- Role names must be Athletic Performance / Athletic Medicine / Applied Performance / Nutrition / Mental Health / Sport Coaches / Leadership. build.js rejects others.
- Keep semicolons out of `trust.limitations` entries; the posts join them with "; ".
- Deck fonts: Agency FB (ships with Office on Windows) and Baylor Bears Font (installed per user at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Fonts` on this laptop only; copies in `DEV/Baylor_Fonts`). Install both before building on the Mac. Neither has an italic face.
- Bears is OpenType-CFF, so PowerPoint cannot embed it: the PDF draws Bears text as outlines and labels the hidden text layer "Calibri". That Calibri is expected, not a fallback. publish.ps1 checks only that Agency FB is embedded.
- Bears has no `? , ' ( ) % / < + ° ±`. Keep `headline` to letters, numbers, spaces, `. : ! - #`; build.js falls back to Agency FB bold for other display text.
- Agency FB has no `→`; it falls back to Calibri. Prefer "to".
- pptxgenjs does not shrink text to fit. Shorten the words rather than raising limits without re-checking the slide PNGs.
- publish.ps1 needs PowerPoint COM (Windows). If PowerPoint has a dialog open, export fails: close it and rerun.
- Revisions: bump `version` in review.json so `_vN` files are added, not overwritten.
- Cite printed journal pages, not PDF positions. The verifier maps Zotero's PDF pages to printed pages itself (`source.printed_offset`, `TypeSafe_Sandbox` PR #19). Cite the page where a table or number is printed, not the page whose text discusses it; that mix-up was all 7 of #002's bad citations. Still say in notes.md which page numbering it uses.

1. Eric: share the Drive folder with Joe (edit access), and tell him to open `START HERE.txt`.
2. Wait for Joe's field notes for lessons 0001 and 0002, then write lesson 0003
   (the three constraint classes) with `/teach`. Re-run the export after it.

- Lessons say "ask the agent"; the export swaps that for "ask Eric". Keep it that way
  unless Joe gets Claude.
- Keep the book PDF and OCR text local and ignored by Git. Do not scan pages 254 onward.
  Do not run a second book ingest.
- Velocity-band sheet: readings above 10.5 m/s are discarded, and Catapult HSD/sprint
  bands are relative to profile MV. See the script docstring.
- On Windows, `git worktree remove` / `prune` can fail with "Permission denied".
  This is not a file lock. The folders carry a **read-only attribute**, probably set by
  Drive sync. Leave the worktree first, then run, from the repo root:
  `attrib -r /s /d .git\worktrees\<name>` and `attrib -r /s /d .claude\worktrees\<name>`,
  then `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force` both folders and `git worktree prune`.
  Before deleting, confirm every file in the worktree is already in git history.
  Found 2026-09-26.

    and it names any `[REVIEW]` claims a person still has to read), **FAIL** (exit 1,
    blocks), **DEGRADED** (exit 2, warns and lets the publish through).
  - **DEGRADED deliberately does not block.** The check needs a sibling clone, a venv,
    a key and a network; a gate that stops the week's deliverable because a different
    repo is missing is a gate that gets deleted. WORKFLOW.md requires reporting it.

    **FABRICATED, exit 1, blocked.** With the verifier hidden: **DEGRADED, exit 2, not
    blocked.** Both scripts parse clean.

    level up.** AGENTS.md tells a background session to work in `.claude/worktrees/`,
    where the parent is `.claude/worktrees`, not DEV - assuming the depth would have
    broken the check in the setup this project uses most.
  - Limit worth knowing: only claims that **cite a page** take the numeric string-match
    path. A fabricated number in uncited prose (`did.facts`, `trust.sample`) goes to the
    prose path and can land in `review` rather than `fabricated`. Found while testing
    this wiring; it is a property of the verifier, not of the gate.

The authors do state "less than one degree" in words on p. 6, so it is defensible, but the "biggest gap" framing is ours. The readout now uses the authors' wording; v4 still uses ours.

- **`review.json` needs `paper.zotero_key` or the verifier cannot run at all.**
  `verify.py` exits immediately on an empty key, so a review built from a source that
  was never imported — like #002, built from Europe PMC XML — silently has no gate at

# AGENTS.md

Project: S2_Evaluation


## Session routine
- Start: run `git pull`, then read docs/STATUS.md before doing anything else.
- End: update docs/STATUS.md (done, next, open questions), commit, and `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

## Source of truth

This folder is the source of truth for S2 Cognition work. The Claude cloud project
"S2 Cognition" is only a pointer to here. Durable notes go in `docs/` and get
committed.

## Read first

| Doc | When |
|---|---|
| `CONTEXT.md` | Always. Project language and the Beyond Percentiles framing. |
| `docs/STATUS.md` | Always, at session start. |
| `docs/program/executive-report.md` | Team-wide and position-group findings, 2021-2024, with benchmarks and flagged players. |
| `docs/program/analysis-strategy.md` | Planning an analysis or a coach-facing report. Includes the translate-to-football-language table. |
| `docs/program/implementation-plan.md` | Rolling out to staff: the 8-week, five-phase plan. |
| `docs/program/literature-review.md` | Background on the nine skills, validation research, position benchmarks, LSU and C.J. Stroud case studies. |
| `docs/program/citations-and-data-sources.md` | Sourcing a claim, or checking a known limitation of the dataset. |
| `docs/program/coaches-playbook.md` | Prescribing a drill for a cognitive weakness. S2's position-by-position quick fixes and drill concepts. |
| `docs/program/external-research-summary.md` | Short version of the outside research, including the LSU numbers and position thresholds. |
| `docs/adr/` | Why a methodological decision was made. Read before relitigating one. |

## Where related work lives

- `COG_S2_Position_Reports/` in `~/DEV` holds the per-position S2 report PDFs.
- `data/` holds athlete-level scores. It is gitignored and lives on Google Drive (`04_RESEARCH/03_Active_Studies/S2_Evaluation/data`, see `docs/program/README_DATA.md`); the repo-local `data/` is a fallback.
- `figures/` is tracked in git, but only for aggregate charts that name no athlete.
  Anything per-athlete, including a chart whose title or filename carries a name, goes
  in `data/` instead. Check every image before committing it.
- Deliverables go to `00_Primary_Storage_Drive` on Google Drive, not into this repo.

## Rules

- Never overwrite an existing file. Create a new one.
- `data/` holds identifiable athlete scores. Never paste its contents into chat, an
  artifact, or an external service. Access is need-to-know staff only.
- Read credentials from `.env` on disk. Never paste a key into chat and never echo a
  value.
- Third-party platforms stay read-only: navigate and read, do not edit.
- Writing style: plain and direct. No em dashes, no corporate language. Post-process
  documents through the humanizer and articulation skills.
- Documents use the Baylor design system (spec in the Brand & Design System section of
  `07_EDUCATION/2026_AppliedNewsletter/CLAUDE.md` on the primary storage drive).
- Working year is 2025 unless a document says otherwise.

## Working across Claude Code and Cowork

Both read this folder. Anything durable, a decision, a finding, a handoff, goes in
`docs/` and gets committed in the same session it was learned. Nothing durable stays
in a chat transcript.

---

## Tensions and contradictions

Status after the interview (2026-09-28): resolved 1 (partly), 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9; still open 7 (partly), 8, 10. New tensions from the interview are 11 to 16. Each entry below carries its status on its last line.

1. **The task's own premise doesn't fully hold.** Both class transcripts (Class 1 and Class 3) are diarized entirely under a single Fireflies speaker label, "Chris Ruf," for every line — including Class 3, which the Spring 2026 teaching schedule assigns solo to Rash (`spring-2026-teaching.md`: "Feb. 5 | Conditioning - Alactic-Aerobic | Rash"). Fireflies likely defaulted to the meeting organizer's name instead of doing real per-speaker diarization. This means roughly 30,000 words of the richest, most first-person material in this corpus cannot be confidently attributed to Rash specifically versus Ruf or Wenger. Every transcript-sourced bullet above is marked Inferred for this reason, even where the underlying statement is a confident, first-person claim.
   **Status (interview 2026-09-28): partly resolved.** Q1 claimed four positions (Vermeil hierarchy, undulating periodization, Dynamic Correspondence, the football energy-system stack), now Explicit. Every other transcript bullet stays Inferred.

2. **Department reporting model is not internally consistent.** The Playbook (p.6) frames Applied Performance as a peer discipline inside Health & Wellness that "enables" Athletics Performance, Athletic Medicine, Nutrition, and Mental Health to answer their own questions. But Week 1 course material lists "Applied Performance" as one of many training sub-categories nested under Athletic Performance itself (p.11), and the same transcript narration describes Rash's role as "helping program and plan the training" — a support-staff framing, not a peer-department framing. Which model actually governs day-to-day authority is not reconciled anywhere in these documents.
   **Status (interview 2026-09-28): resolved.** Eric (Q5): "Both." Both framings are true at once.

3. **Coach's-eye-first versus objective-first is argued both ways.** The course material repeatedly argues that "you don't need a fancy test... you have to have a good coach's eye" and criticizes the GPS/load-monitoring era for breeding a fear-driven under-training culture. Eric's own SportSmith writing moves the opposite direction on daily monitoring specifically: he replaced subjective wellness surveys with objective force-plate mRSI because subjective self-report couldn't be trusted. Both share a skepticism of trendy or convenient data, but they land on opposite defaults (trust the trained eye vs. require an objective number) for the daily-monitoring question specifically.
   **Status (interview 2026-09-28): resolved.** Eric (Q6): the coach's eye flags where to look; data then investigates. The two are sequential, not rival defaults.

4. **The Assessment Manual (V12) reads as an older document than the current technology stack.** It builds its 1RM-estimation protocol around GymAware, and its CMJ description references a "contact mat" for jump height. The current Playbook technology stack and the Development Plan both center velocity-based training on Perch, not GymAware, and the current Force Plate Testing V3 protocol runs all CMJ variants exclusively on ForceDecks force plates, with no contact mat mentioned. This suggests the Assessment Manual predates the current VALD/Perch-centered stack and may be a legacy document rather than the currently operative protocol — worth confirming directly with Eric before treating any of its specifics as current practice.
   **Status (interview 2026-09-28): resolved.** Eric (Q8): V12 "is not current"; a new manual built on the NCAA technology and sport-science recommendations is in development. All V12 bullets are marked Legacy.

5. **Testing cueing instructions conflict across two protocol documents for the same test.** The Assessment Manual's CMJ instructions say explicitly: "Do not coach the strategy of jumping." The current Force Plate Testing V3 protocol gives testers specific verbal cues to give athletes during CMJ, squat-jump, and hop-test administration ("keep chest up," "land softly," "land stiff-legged on only the toes"). These may be reconcilable (safety/technique cues vs. jump-strategy cues are different things), but the two documents read differently on how much a tester should say out loud.
   **Status (interview 2026-09-28): resolved by Q8.** Inference: with V12 not current, the Force Plate Testing V3 cues govern. Eric did not address the cueing question itself.

6. **Two different anaerobic-threshold heart-rate methods appear back to back in the same slide deck without being reconciled.** One slide gives an age-based formula (max HR = 220-age for men, 226-age for women, threshold at ~85% of that), and the very next slides give a body-size-based table (big/medium/small athlete, ~165/170/175 bpm threshold) as the operational standard used elsewhere throughout the conditioning material. Which one is actually used day to day is not stated. [class-4-2026.md pp.27-29]
   **Status (interview 2026-09-28): resolved.** Eric (Q20): "Age-based." The body-size table is marked Superseded. Note that the body-size table was from Eric's own assigned session, so his slides and his practice differ.

7. **The Development Plan's own critique cuts against the corpus it's part of.** It states the current Baylor Playbook "has no educational component whatsoever" and reads "like a vendor product reference manual," even though Eric personally co-teaches a full graduate-level course covering much of the same material the Playbook is missing. The department's teaching capacity clearly exists; it just hasn't been captured back into the Playbook or a formal intern curriculum yet.
   **Status (interview 2026-09-28): still open, confirmed.** Eric (Q30): the intern curriculum "has not been built yet."

8. **The Playbook's NordBord documentation has not caught up with practice.** The Playbook's Technology Overview and Workflows still document a full, unqualified, roster-style NordBord data-collection SOP. # CATES, Comprehensive Athletic Talent Evaluation System

A data-driven system for evaluating collegiate athletes and recruits, built to support
fit determinations and financial decisions on athlete market value and recruitment
investment. Emphasizes NCAA compliance while giving a competitive advantage through
evidence-based assessment.

## Framework

Four pillars, weighted:

| Pillar | Weight | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| Physical Performance | 35% | Testing metrics, force plate, GPS, speed |
| Historical Analysis | 25% | Academic, health, and performance records |
| Cognitive Assessment | 25% | S2 Cognition and related testing |
| Social Intelligence | 15% | Character, fit, locker room factors |

Medical risk is assessed separately on an A-F grading scale and layered over the
weighted score.

## Stakeholders

Athletic department administrators, financial decision-makers, and supervisors.
They need executive-level materials with clear ROI justification and an
implementation path, not raw analytics.

## Current state

The framework and a full executive presentation package exist, covering financial
projections, implementation strategy, and stakeholder communication. The system
supports two intake speeds: a rapid process for time-limited evaluations (transfer
portal, incoming grad athletes) and a comprehensive process for full comparative
analytics.

## Working notes

- Success measures: recruitment efficiency, reduced injury-related cost, performance outcomes
- Standardized athlete profiles are the unit of comparison
- Transfer portal and incoming graduate athlete evaluation are the highest-value use cases

## Repo layout

- `docs/`: decision records, methodology, framework documentation
- `docs/program/`: the framework documents moved off the cloud project
- `data/`: pointer only. See `data/README.md`.

No source files existed on the primary storage drive when this repo was created.
Content lived in the Claude cloud project only. Add materials here as they are built.

## Related

- S2_Evaluation (cognitive testing that feeds the Cognitive Assessment pillar)
- PlayerProfiles_FB_03-28-2026 (athlete profiling)

## Read first

This repo is the source of truth. The Cowork project "Athlete Evaluation Framework" is
only a pointer.

| Read | When |
|---|---|
| `docs/STATUS.md` | Every session, first thing |
| `docs/program/README.md` | To see what moved off the cloud project and what did not |
| `docs/program/comprehensive-athletic-talent-evaluation-system.md` | Current system definition, five weighted components |
| `docs/program/comprehensive-athlete-evaluation-system.md` | Original CAES four-pillar framework, kept for lineage |
| `docs/program/rapid-athletic-cognitive-assessment-protocol.md` | Portal or group evaluation under time pressure |
| `docs/program/executive-white-paper.md` | Stakeholder and ROI conversations |
| `docs/program/baylor-medical-grading-rubric.md` | The A-F medical grade layered over the weighted score |
| `docs/context.md` | Principles and approach carried over from the cloud project |

## Where related code and data live

- `~/DEV/S2_Evaluation`: cognitive testing that feeds the Cognitive Assessment pillar
- `~/DEV/PlayerProfiles_FB_03-28-2026`: football athlete profiling
- `~/DEV/COG_S2_Position_Reports`: S2 position reporting
- `~/DEV/SportScienceResearchRepo/SourcePapers/`: the total-score-of-athleticism literature
- Deliverables (.docx, .pptx, spreadsheets) go to `00_Primary_Storage_Drive` on Google Drive, not this repo
- Athlete-level data goes on the primary storage drive, never in this repo. See `data/README.md`

## Project rules

- Always create new files. Never overwrite an existing one.
- Default to 2025 as the working year in documents unless stated otherwise.
- Credentials come from `.env` on disk. Never pasted into chat, never echoed.
- Third-party platforms stay read-only.
- Baylor design system on every document. Spec in AGENTS.md.
- Financial figures in the white paper are unverified projections. Do not restate them as findings.

End: update `docs/STATUS.md`, commit, `git push`.
